entities.summary: Marcus Valerius Messalla Appianus was a Roman Senator during the reign of Augustus, serving as ordinary consul in 12 BC alongside Publius Sulpicius Quirinius. Appianus' significance lies in his role as a key figure in the Roman Senate, where he played a role in shaping the Empire's governance and politics. His involvement in the Roman Senate spanned multiple decades, with notable mentions including his role in the construction of the Aqua Appia, a significant water supply project that improved the quality of life for Roman citizens. The legacy of Marcus Valerius Messalla Appianus can be seen in the continued influence of Roman governance and politics on modern Western societies. Notably, his involvement in the Roman Senate predates the rise of Christianity, highlighting the complex interplay between religion and politics in ancient Rome. The impact of Appianus' role in the Roman Senate can be seen in the subsequent development of the Roman Imperial system, which continues to shape modern governance and politics. The legacy of Marcus Valerius Messalla Appianus serves as a testament to the enduring power of Roman governance and politics, shaping the course of Western history. Through his involvement in the Roman Senate, Appianus played a pivotal role in shaping the trajectory of Roman governance and politics, leaving an indelible mark on the course of Western history.
